page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-64 is a memory-oriented server profile within the N2 family, configured with 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores and 512 GB of system RAM. Based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon platform operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, this configuration provides an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU). The processor includes dedicated core allocation, hyperthreading, a 33 MB L3 cache, and instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA. This instance type includes no local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate solid mid-range compute efficiency alongside distinct strengths in select high-throughput multi-threaded tasks. Stress-ng scores reached 1,839.98 in single-core and 60,212.33 in multi-core metrics, falling within the middle 50% tier. Geekbench software compilation with Clang scored 40,780.0, and image processing registered at 14,883.0, both placing in the top 25% bracket. Memory subsystem performance shows a large-block read bandwidth of 162.21 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 70.36 GB/sec, supporting Redis SET throughput of 53.97 million operations per second and static web throughput of 36.1 GB/sec.

Tradeoffs center around memory capacity versus compute density and storage topology. Because local storage is absent, all persistent data workloads require external block storage attachments. Additionally, while the large 512 GB memory footprint allows in-memory loading of substantial parameter spaces, LLM text generation against large 70B models achieves only 2.56 tokens per second, falling into the bottom 25% due to the lack of dedicated hardware acceleration. Cost efficiency is defined by high memory density per compute thread rather than raw floating-point operations.
The n2-highmem-64 is primarily suited for large in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, memory-intensive continuous integration builds, data analytics, and large ETL batch pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-64 is a high-memory configuration featuring 64 vCPUs across 32 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.8 GHz and 512 GB of RAM, offering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 vector extensions, AES cryptography, and a 33 MB L3 cache. It contains no onboard GPUs and provides no bundled local storage. Benchmarks place the system in the middle 50% for general stress-ng CPU runs and overall PassMark metrics, while software compilation and image processing demonstrate top 25% performance. Memory throughput supports up to 162.21 GB/sec for uncached reads and 53.97 million Redis SET operations per second. However, CPU-based large language model execution remains weak for large 70B parameter generation (2.56 tokens/sec). The server is technically matched for in-memory databases, large cache clusters, Clang build farms, and memory-heavy ETL processing.
og_description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-64 features 64 vCPUs, 512 GB RAM, and an Intel Xeon 2.8 GHz base. It delivers strong memory bandwidth and Clang compile speeds for memory-bound workloads.

tagline: 64 dedicated vCPUs with 512 GB memory for high-capacity in-memory databases, intensive caching tiers, and multi-threaded compilation workloads.

512 GB system memory (8 GB per vCPU allocation)
Hardware vector support including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI
Strong compilation performance scoring in the top 25% for Clang
